b.d: German maker of the Virus virtual-analogue synth line.
Ittervoort maker of timpani, marimbas, xylophones, vibraphones and brass, founded by André Adams.
Audio Engineering Associates, founded by Wes Dooley and Bob Gerbracht to service RCA ribbons; makes the R44C.
Maker of the Pianola (1896) and the Duo-Art reproducing piano (1914).
Pro-audio brand descended from Japan's Akai, best known for the MPC.
Vienna maker of the C12, C414 and D12, part of Harman since 1994.
Santa Rosa, California maker of neck-through basses with active electronics, founded by Owsley Stanley, Ron Wickersham, Rick Turner and Bob Matthews.
Keith Barr's company, part of inMusic since 2012.
Carlsfeld bandoneon and concertina factory founded by Ernst Alfred Arnold (1873–1933).
English mixing-console maker from Penryn, Cornwall, part of Audiotonix; Xone is its DJ line.
Houston, Texas supplier of necks, bodies, hardware, pickguards and electronics.
Pioneer's former DJ division, independent since 2014 and renamed AlphaTheta Corporation in 2020; owned by Noritsu.
Cremona family (c. 1538–1740) whose founder Andrea Amati fixed the form of violin, viola and cello; Nicolò taught Stradivari.
Bass-amp maker of the B-15 Portaflex and SVT; part of Yamaha Guitar Group since 2018.
Seville and Almería luthier (1817–1892) who set the form of the modern classical guitar.
Cremona maker (1644–1737) of over 1,100 instruments, about 650 surviving; his model is the most copied.
Ivor Arbiter's London company that launched the Fuzz Face in 1966.
American synth maker founded by Alan R. Pearlman; closed 1981, name revived by Korg.
Grenoble maker founded by Frédéric Brun and Gilles Pommereuil; software emulations and hybrid synths.
Japanese audio maker of turntables and cartridges.
Recorder trademark of Toyama Musical Instruments, used since 1954.
Brass maker founded in New York by trumpeter Vincent Bach; now a Conn-Selmer brand made in Elkhart.
Founded by Uli Behringer in Willich; part of Music Tribe; known for low-cost clones of classic synths.
Robert Benedetto's hand-carved jazz archtops; Savannah facility from 2006.
Brass maker founded in Paris, long based in London and merged with Boosey & Hawkes; now part of Buffet Crampon.
Berlin-founded, Heilbronn-based maker; sold to Cosonic Intelligent in 2025.
Maker of Paul Bigsby's vibrato tailpiece; a Fender subsidiary since 2019.
Italian maker of the magnetic-drum Echorec.
Leipzig piano maker founded by Julius Blüthner, known for aliquot stringing.
Istanbul workshop founded by smiths Hasan Seker, Ibrahim Yakici and Hasan Ozdemir; fully hand-hammered.
Roland-owned brand; made the SP-303 sampler.
Rudy Bozak's company, maker of the first commercial DJ mixer.
Woburn, Massachusetts maker of handmade flutes including the Brögger and Kingma System models.
Founded by Don Buchla in Berkeley, California; assets owned by Buchla U.S.A. since 2018.
Paris clarinet maker founded by Denis Buffet-Auger, based in Mantes-la-Ville; now a group owning several wind brands.
Viennese piano maker founded by Ignaz Bösendorfer; owned by Yamaha since 2008.
Berlin piano maker founded by Carl Bechstein.
Harp maker founded by Gérard and Joël Garnier in Mouzeil near Nantes; lever harps first, pedal harps from 1987.
Electronics maker with Privia and Celviano digital pianos.
Ipswich speaker maker of the Blue, Greenback and Vintage 30; owned by Gold Peak.
Californian hot-rod superstrat maker linked to Jackson; Fender-owned since 2002.
Robert Clarke's Manchester firm, the first factory maker of tin whistles, shown at the 1851 Great Exhibition.
Maker of Nord stage pianos and keyboards.
US maker that claims the original carbon-fibre bow, in Master, Performance and Student tiers.
Coles Electroacoustics, maker of the 4038 since the mid-1970s.
C. G. Conn of Elkhart, Indiana, a leading American maker of brass and saxophones.
Nylon-string guitar brand; its Córdoba Music Group owns Guild.
Farmingdale, New York string and accessory maker; also owns Evans, ProMark and Rico.
John D'Angelico's Little Italy archtop workshop; brand revived in 2011.
London company behind the Rangemaster treble booster of 1965.
Nathan Daniel's New Jersey maker of Masonite guitars with lipstick-tube pickups.
DG Percussion, founded by percussionist Paolo De Gregorio, maker of flamenco cajons.
Brand of Harry DeArmond's pickups and early tremolo units.
DJ equipment brand of Denon, maker of the Prime standalone series.
Maker of the Whammy pitch shifter.
Staten Island-born maker that popularised direct-replacement pickups, starting with the FS-1 and Super Distortion.
Dopyera brothers' spider-bridge resonator brand, owned by Gibson since 1993 and made by Epiphone.
American pedal maker founded by David DiFrancesco; owned by Harman from 1990 and Cortek from 2022.
German maker run by Dieter Döpfer in Gräfelfing; created the Eurorack format.
Venetian maker (1686–1750) of violins, violas, cellos and basses, best known for wide cellos.
Californian maker (DW), known for its 5000 pedal and Collector's Series; owned by Roland since 2022.
Howard Alexander Dumble's Santa Cruz shop; about 300 amps, revived by the Dumble Preservation Society in 2022.
Jim Dunlop's accessories company; owns MXR and the Fuzz Face rights.
Seattle maker of lever harps and hammered dulcimers.
Kolkata firm founded by Dwarkanath Ghose, credited with developing the hand-held Indian harmonium.
Santa Cruz-founded pioneer of samplers and sample-based drum machines.
Mike Matthews's New York City pedal maker; revived via Sovtek after its 1984 closure.
American microphone and loudspeaker maker, a Bosch division since 2006.
Gothenburg maker of step-sequenced instruments.
Coated-string brand of W. L. Gore & Associates.
Santa Rosa, California maker of active pickups, founded by Rob Turner.
American maker of affordable samplers, starting with the Mirage.
Former New York archtop rival bought by Gibson, now its lower-priced brand.
Californian strings company; owner of Music Man since 1984 and maker of the Earthwood acoustic bass.
Tokyo maker of metal-oriented electrics, with LTD as its lower-priced line.
American maker of studio effects processors and pedals.
Eddie Van Halen's brand, made with Fender; carries the 5150 amp name since 2007.
French maker of the Osmose expressive keyboard synth.
Paris oboe maker founded by François Lorée, Triébert's last foreman; makes the whole oboe family.
Sydney maker of the Fairlight CMI sampler-workstation.
Osimo electronics maker formed from three accordion firms, known for the Compact combo organs.
Grand piano maker founded by Paolo Fazioli in Sacile.
Californian maker of the Telecaster and Stratocaster and the first mass-market solid-body electric.
Waltham, Massachusetts glassworks that revived the glass armonica with quartz-glass bowls.
Company of inventor Floyd D. Rose, maker of the double-locking tremolo.
Fox Products Corporation of South Whitley, Indiana, founded by bassoonist Hugo Fox; makes bassoons and oboes.
Cliff Chase's New Hampshire maker of the Axe-Fx rack and FM floor modellers.
French bow maker (1747–1835) whose 1785–1790 changes shaped the modern bow.
Michael Fuller's California pedal maker, known for the OCD; Culver City shop closed in 2022.
Tampa, Florida maker of moulded and padded cases and bags, founded by Jerry Freed and Crystal Morris; owns Levy's Leathers since 2018.
Family firm in Mainz known above all for its horns.
Whistle maker founded by Alfred Brown in Oswestry, Shropshire; brass whistles with moulded mouthpieces.
Family brass maker founded by T. J. Getzen in Elkhorn, Wisconsin.
Michigan-born, Nashville-based maker of the Les Paul, SG, ES-335 and Gibson archtops.
Cremona violin maker (1698–1744) whose labels carried the IHS monogram; his violins rival Stradivari's.
Japanese tuner and bridge maker; makes Kluson-style replicas and the GE1996T tremolo.
Delta, British Columbia maker of TUSQ nuts and saddles, Ratio tuners and String Saver saddles.
New York firm known for flashy hollow bodies and rockabilly guitars.
Ohio tuner company descended from A. D. Grover & Son; name adopted in 1952.
Founded by Alfred Dronge in Manhattan; now part of Córdoba Music Group under Yamaha.
Inventor of the tonewheel organ; company closed 1985, name bought by Suzuki in 1989 (Hammond-Suzuki).
Wilhelm Heckel GmbH of Wiesbaden(-Biebrich), family firm founded by Johann Adam Heckel; inventor of the heckelphone.
Stand brand of the Taiwanese music company KHS, making stands since about 2002.
Guillemot's DJ controller brand.
Munich and Reisbach family workshop; Hauser Sr. (1882–1952) built Segovia's 1937 guitar.
Interlaken, New York maker of bridges, tuners and Xtender drop-tuning keys.
Kolkata sitar maker whose older instruments are collectible.
British maker of lightweight crush-resistant hard cases for guitars and other instruments, made in the UK for over 35 years.
Trossingen instrument maker; built the Clavinet and Pianet.
Wisconsin brass maker best known for its Farkas horns.
Kalimbas named after ethnomusicologist Hugh Tracey, hand-made in a family-run workshop in Grahamstown.
German maker of the 500/1 violin bass.
Hoshino Gakki's brand, central to superstrats and shred guitars.
Canadian maker of Eurorack modules and cases.
Istanbul cymbal maker founded by Agop Tomurcuk, run by his sons Arman and Sarkis since 1996.
St Louis, later Chicago, maker of xylophones, marimbas, vibraharps, chimes and glockenspiels; mark sold to Yamaha in 1986.
eras: Clair Omar Musser, mallet division, from 1930

b.d: Californian metal-guitar maker of the Soloist and Rhoads; Fender-owned since 2002.
Mirecourt-born Paris maker (1798–1875) whose workshop made over 3,000 instruments, famed for Stradivari and Guarneri copies and bows.
Speaker maker of the alnico P10R and C12 series fitted to tweed-era Fender amps.
Josh Scott's pedal company, known for Tube Screamer and RAT derivatives and the 3 Series.
König & Meyer of Wertheim am Main, founded by Karl König and Erich Meyer; music, instrument and microphone stands.
Maker of the cam-based Kahler Tremolo System.
Honolulu ukulele maker founded by Samuel Kamaka Sr.; inventor of the pineapple ukulele.
Hamamatsu piano maker founded by Koichi Kawai.
Julius Keilwerth of Nauheim, German saxophone maker known for the SX90R.
Christoph Kemper's German brand, maker of the Profiler, introduced in 2011.
Brand of the H. N. White Company of Cleveland, Ohio, known for the Zephyr and Super 20 saxophones.
Bill Finnegan's Boston pedal maker, known for the Centaur and the KTR.
Chicago tuner maker whose Deluxe machines were standard on 1950s–60s Fenders; brand revived by WD Music in 1993.
Finnish kantele maker known for concert kanteles and an electric kantele with guitar-style pickups.
Japanese electronic instrument maker, owner of the ARP name since its 2015 reissues.
1980s superstrat leader, now a Gibson brand.
Kaufman, Texas family firm of Milton Kyser, maker of the trigger-style Quick-Change capo.
Schaffhausen recorder maker founded by Franz Küng.
London concertina maker of Louis Lachenal, who built for Wheatstone from 1848; Lachenal & Co. closed around 1933.
Martin Cohen's New York firm, maker of congas, bongos, cajons and inventor of the Vibraslap; owned by Drum Workshop since 2014.
Indianapolis drum maker that introduced the vibraphone; sold to Conn in 1929, rights now with Gretsch.
Rotating-speaker cabinets invented by Donald Leslie; Electro Music sold to CBS in 1965, bought by Suzuki in 1992.
Calabasas maker of the POD and Helix modellers; owned by Yamaha since 2014.
Roger Linn's company that made the LM-1 and LinnDrum.
Violist who designed the 16¾-inch Tertis model viola.
George Lowden's workshop, family-run in Downpatrick, County Down, since 2004.
Chicago home-organ maker founded on Frederick C. Lowrey's designs; owned by Kawai from 1988, production ended 2019.
Chicago-founded drum maker, now in Monroe, North Carolina; Ringo Starr's kit maker; part of Conn-Selmer.
Chicago harp maker, founded as a sheet-music shop; first harp 1889; subsidiary of Salvi Harps since 1987.
Canadian maker of synthetic woodwind reeds.
Gibson's effects brand, maker of the first commercial fuzz pedal, the FZ-1 Fuzz-Tone of 1962.
American Eurorack maker based in Asheville, North Carolina.
American music stand maker whose stand was designed by inventor and musician Otto Lagervall; known for the Symphony stand.
Founded in Paris as Strasser Marigaux & Lemaire (SML); oboes only since 1981.
Arcata, California maker of concert marimbas and xylophones.
Maker of about 9 million inexpensive plastic ukuleles, late 1940s to late 1960s.
British amplifier maker whose pedals include the Guv'nor and ShredMaster.
Jim Marshall's London firm, maker of the JTM45, Plexi and JCM800 and the 4x12 stack.
Flat-top maker founded in New York and based in Nazareth, Pennsylvania, since 1839; originator of the dreadnought and OM.
Nisshin Onpa's brand; designed and built the original Tube Screamer and sells its own OD-808.
Percussion maker founded by Roland Meinl in Gutenstetten; its Byzance B20 cymbals are made in Turkey.
Tuba brand of Melton Meinl Weston in Geretsried, part of Buffet Crampon since 2012.
Randall Smith's California maker of the Mark series and Rectifier; bought by Gibson in 2021.
Cooperative instrument maker in Waldkraiburg, Bavaria, known for tubas.
Flute maker founded by Masashi Miyazawa; known for the Improved Scale and Brögger System.
Celle recorder maker and publisher founded by Hermann Moeck.
Fulda woodwind family firm founded by Johann Andreas Mollenhauer; recorders include Adri's Dream.
Design-led case and bag brand founded in San Francisco, now headquartered in Singapore, known for the M80 Vertigo case.
Founded as R. A. Moog Co. by Robert Moog; based in Asheville, North Carolina; owned by inMusic since 2023.
Flute maker founded by Koichi Muramatsu; factory in Tokorozawa.
Maker of the StingRay; owned by Ernie Ball since 1984 (Ernie Ball Music Man); Sterling by Music Man is its lower-cost line.
Fort Atkinson, Wisconsin maker of musical saws, still producing in 2000.
Mallet-instrument maker founded by Clair Omar Musser after leaving Deagan; owned by Ludwig since 1965.
Émilie Gillet's open-source Eurorack module maker; closed December 2022.
Rochester, New York, pedal maker founded by Keith Barr and Terry Sherwood; owned by Dunlop since 1987.
National String Instrument Corporation, maker of the tricone; revived as National Reso-Phonic in San Luis Obispo.
Berlin maker of music software and the Maschine system.
Berlin-founded studio microphone maker, owned by Sennheiser since 1991.
Helsinki maker of Archetype plug-ins and the Quad Cortex floor modeller.
British maker of MIDI controllers, synthesizers and the Circuit grooveboxes.
American DJ equipment brand, part of inMusic.
American synth maker founded by Tom Oberheim.
Cliff Cooper's London maker known for orange covering and picture-symbol controls.
Danish cartridge maker founded in Copenhagen.
Kaman-founded maker of roundback guitars with composite bowls, New Hartford, Connecticut.
Bernard Overton's workshop, which recreated the low whistle for Finbar Furey.
Cymbal maker founded in Saint Petersburg, now in Nottwil, Switzerland; pioneered B8 '2002 Bronze' and Signature Bronze.
Bern firm of Felix Rohner and Sabina Schärer (PANArt Hangbau AG) that created the Hang.
Castelfidardo maker, the first Italian accordion company.
Japanese drum maker whose Export is the best-selling drum set line.
American amplifier maker; made the 5150 for Eddie Van Halen, later sold as the 6505.
Nashville pedalboard maker, described in the trade press as the most popular pedalboard brand.
Saw factory in Kausala, Finland, making the Speliplari musical saw.
Paris piano maker founded by Ignace Pleyel; production stopped in 2013 and resumed under Algam in 2017.
Leipzig disc music box maker founded by Brachhausen and Riessner; Polyphon-Musikwerke AG from 1895.
Flute maker founded in Boston by Verne Q. Powell, now in Maynard, Massachusetts; owned by Buffet Crampon since 2016.
ProCo Sound, maker of the RAT distortion since 1978.
Drumstick maker acquired by D'Addario in 2011.
Paul Reed Smith's Maryland maker of carved-top double-cutaways.
Madrid guitar workshop; first major maker to use cedar tops (1965).
Audio maker from Mukilteo, Washington, owned by inMusic since 2016.
American electronics company that made the first mass-produced theremin in 1929.
New Jersey disc music box maker founded by Gustave Brachhausen; music boxes shipped 1892–1921.
German DJ equipment brand.
Sainte-Croix maker of music boxes, singing birds and musical watches; music boxes from Albert Reuge's workshop.
Electric piano brand of Harold Rhodes, made with Fender from 1965.
Californian maker of jangly 300-series semi-hollows and 12-strings.
French oboe and cor anglais maker in Saint-Maur-des-Fossés, bought by Buffet Crampon in 2019.
Delhi sitar maker whose older instruments are collectible.
British engineer and pedal maker known for the Octavia.
Historic American drum maker, later a revived brand.
Electronic musical instrument maker.
1970s pedal brand revived in 2018 with a reissued Compressor.
Sevenoaks, Kent string maker founded by James How.
Ribbon microphone maker founded by David Royer.
Cymbal maker founded by Robert Zildjian in Meductic, New Brunswick, after the Zildjian family split.
Harp maker founded by Victor Salvi in Genoa, based in Piasco since 1974; owns Lyon & Healy and Bow Brand.
Swedish steel and tool group whose Stradivarius saw is the classic Scandinavian musical saw.
Accordion maker begun by Silvio Scandalli at Camerano; part of Farfisa from 1946, accordion-only brand since 1984.
German hardware maker that built the Floyd Rose Original from 1983 to 2024.
Californian maker best known today for modern metal guitars.
Chicago-area maker founded by Chicago Symphony trumpeter Renold Schilke.
Founded by Gerhard Priel and Bengt Schumacher, first making slit drums, now a major cajón maker.
Budapest workshop of V. József Schunda, designer of the concert cimbalom (1874); over 10,000 made by 1906.
French firm that made Mario Maccaferri's guitar from 1932 to about 1952.
Wedemark audio maker founded by Fritz Sennheiser; parent of Neumann.
Founded by Dave Smith as Sequential Circuits in San Francisco; owned by Focusrite since 2021.
C. A. Seydel Söhne of Trossingen, a harmonica business by 1855 and the only one of that era still trading.
Santa Barbara pickup maker founded by Seymour W. Duncan and Cathy Carter Duncan; also makes pedals.
Japanese maker, earlier called Honey, of the Uni-Vibe designed by Fumio Mieda.
Maker of lever-operated capos with an adjustable pressure screw, including a fifth-string banjo capo.
Chicago maker of the Unidyne, SM57, SM58 and SM7.
Dave Simmons' company, maker of the hexagonal-pad SDS-V; name later owned by Guitar Center.
Moulded polymer case maker founded by Dave Sanderson and Steve Kottman, starting with guitar cases; based in Orange, California.
Chicago drum maker of the Radio King; owned by DW since 2019.
London maker linked to Macari's, originator of the Tone Bender and the Colorsound range.
German drum maker in Bad Berleburg, part of KHS.
Fender-owned budget brand making Fender designs in Asia.
Ned Steinberger's maker of graphite headless basses; owned by Gibson since 1987.
Bayreuth family piano maker founded by Eduard Steingraeber.
Piano maker founded in Manhattan by Henry E. Steinway, with factories in New York and Hamburg.
California pedal maker, originally Damage Control Engineering.
Japanese harmonica maker; sells keyboard harmonicas as the Melodion.
First maker of disc-playing music boxes; partners included Brachhausen, Riessner and Paul Lochmann.
Japanese guitar maker known for acoustic-electrics.
Hoshino Gakki's drum brand, made in Seto, Japan and China.
Founded by Bob Taylor and Kurt Listug in El Cajon, California; known for the NT neck and V-Class bracing.
Panasonic's audio brand, maker of the SL-1200 DJ turntable.
Stockholm maker of the OP-1 and Pocket Operators.
Berlin electronics firm whose ELA M 250/251 derived from the AKG C 12.
German music retailer selling budget instruments under its own name.
Japanese harmonica maker that makes the Lee Oskar harmonica.
Paris reed maker founded by clarinettist Eugène Van Doren.
Boston-founded stick maker, now in Holbrook, Massachusetts; Vater-branded sticks since 1990.
Boston maker founded by Julius and Carl Nelson; name owned by Deering since 1989.
Tokyo maker of DJ mixers, turntables and controllers, founded by Hidesato Shiino; bankrupt in 2014.
Drumstick maker from Massachusetts; merged with Zildjian in 2010.
British maker of the Continental combo organ; brand owned by Korg since 1992.
German-system bassoon and contrabassoon brand, part of Buffet Crampon since 2010.
Maker of affordable recreations of classic microphones such as the WA-47 and WA-87 R2.
Pacific Northwest maker of replacement guitar and bass necks and bodies, formerly Boogie Bodies.
Bass maker founded by Hans-Peter Wilfer in Erlangen, based in Markneukirchen since 1995; lines from German Custom Shop to Chinese-made RockBass.
Guitar maker whose AB-40 and AB-20 acoustic basses were popular from the late 1980s.
London firm of Charlie Watkins, maker of the Copicat tape echo.
Maker of the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano (1904).
C. Wheatstone & Co., the firm of Charles Wheatstone, who patented the English concertina in 1829.
America's oldest flute maker, founded in Boston by William S. and George W. Haynes; owned by Eastman since 2004.
Maker of reed electric pianos from 1954 to 1983; bought by Baldwin in 1987.
Japanese instrument giant whose electric lines include the Pacifica and Revstar.
Japanese saxophone specialist, maker of Japan's first soprano and the 90x/99x and WO lines.
Zachary Vex's Minneapolis pedal maker, founded in the mid-1990s; known for the Fuzz Factory.
Cymbal maker founded by Avedis Zildjian in Constantinople, in the US since 1928–29; now in Norwell, Massachusetts.
Paris maker founded by Sébastien Érard, inventor of the double escapement action (1823).
